neighbours.label: first-hand experiential judgments of how a product or place feels, sounds or performs in use (feels, rides smoothly, surprisingly comfortable, much quieter, a huge difference), as against factual specs, price or logistics
fire: After a week with the new mattress, I wake up feeling noticeably less stiff.
The hatchback corners nimbly and the steering feels light in town.
This kettle is surprisingly quiet compared with our old one.
The trail shoes feel cushioned and grippy even on wet rock.
Since we added the rug, the room sounds much warmer and less echoey.
The keyboard has a satisfying, smooth feel when you type fast.
Honestly the cabin is so calm at speed that conversations feel effortless.
The new pillows made a real difference to how well I sleep.
quiet: The new mattress was delivered on Tuesday in a vacuum-sealed box.
The hatchback comes with a 1.2-litre engine and a five-year warranty.
This kettle holds 1.7 litres and costs twenty-five pounds.
The trail shoes are sold in six sizes and three colours.
We bought the rug online and it arrived rolled in plastic.
The keyboard connects over Bluetooth and charges with a USB-C cable.
The cabin has four doors, five seats and a sunroof option.
The new pillows were ordered from a shop in Leeds last month.

predictions: fire 0.5-1.1 on the experiential word; spec/price/shipping sentences below 0.1
notes: Card: peaks on ' difference', ' dynamics', ' feel', ' surprisingly', ' quieter', ' smoothly' in reviews; the - pole is symptoms/skin. Probe: 'huge difference in how quiet' 1.129, 'rides smoothly and feels planted' 1.046, 'surprisingly comfortable' 0.757, 'much quieter' 0.476, 'does feel good' 0.481; price/colours 0.018, box contents 0.050, installation 0.010.
